definitions.explanation: The foot or leg on the right side of the body. As with {足|あし} in general, this can refer to either the foot only or the whole leg depending on context.

examples.japanese: {右足|みぎあし}でボールを{蹴|け}った。
examples.english: I kicked the ball with my right foot.

examples.japanese: {転|ころ}んで{右足|みぎあし}の{足首|あしくび}を{捻挫|ねんざ}してしまい、{一週間|いっしゅうかん}{松葉杖|まつばづえ}{生活|せいかつ}になった。
examples.english: I fell and sprained my right ankle, ending up on crutches for a week.

notes:
Compound of {右|みぎ} (right) + {足|あし} (foot/leg). Like {足|あし}, can mean either the foot only or the whole leg.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {右足|みぎあし}でける: to kick with the right foot
- {右足|みぎあし}を{出|だ}す: to put the right foot forward; to take a step
- {右足|みぎあし}を{骨折|こっせつ}する: to break one's right leg
- {右足|みぎあし}{首|くび}: right ankle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {左足|ひだりあし}: left foot/leg — the symmetric counterpart
- {右脚|みぎあし}: written with {脚|あし} to specifically mean the leg (not foot)
- {利|き}き{足|あし}: dominant foot
